title: LottieFiles Web & Marketing
summary: Reshaped LottieFiles’ web presence into a clearer, more cohesive expression of the brand and its motion ecosystem.
description: I led the design and visual direction of LottieFiles’ web presence while contributing to the broader evolution of the brand. The work began with the homepage and Animation pages, followed later by the Lottie Creator landing page. Across these foundational experiences, I shaped the information architecture, UX, UI, interaction, motion, and shared design patterns that established the standard for future marketing pages. As the direction expanded, I guided other designers on how to apply and extend the system, led stakeholder reviews, and improved the design-to-launch process. Pages were aligned in Figma before being implemented in Framer, and I held final design approval for structure, consistency, and visual quality before updates were released.

insights.label: Why it mattered
insights.body: LottieFiles had grown into a broad ecosystem, but its web presence lacked a consistent story and shared visual language across products and audiences.

insights.label: Key decision
insights.body: Instead of treating each page as a separate campaign, I established reusable visual, structural, and interaction patterns that could evolve across pages and teams.

insights.label: Organizational impact
insights.body: The direction became the standard used by other designers. Design reviews and final QA helped Brand, Product, Marketing, and Engineering maintain consistency as the web presence expanded.

whatScaled: The new brand and web direction set a higher standard for visual design and motion across LottieFiles. Its shared patterns, review process, and quality bar guided the marketing pages that followed.

title: LottieFiles Digital Asset Management
summary: Expanded LottieFiles Platform into a multi-format asset workspace and delivery system.
description:
I led the UX, UI, and product workflows that expanded LottieFiles Platform to support images, SVGs, videos, and source files alongside animations. I used AI to rapidly build an early proof of concept, aligning stakeholders, Product, and Engineering on the shared model and workflows before moving into high-fidelity design.

Rather than creating a separate destination, I integrated these formats into the organization, status, review, approval, versioning, and delivery workflows teams already understood. I also improved everyday asset management through multi-format and folder uploads, multi-file copy and paste, and drag-and-drop organization. I defined the core Platform experience, guided its adaptation for the plugins, and designed the corresponding experience in Lottie Creator, where I also contributed to front-end implementation.

insights.label: Why it mattered
insights.body: Team and Enterprise customers, internal product teams, and motion designers were managing related assets across multiple services. This made complete projects harder to organize, track, and deliver.

insights.label: Key decision
insights.body: The new formats became part of the existing asset model rather than a separate product area. Shared behaviors stayed consistent, while previews, metadata, and actions adapted to each format.

insights.label: Outcome
insights.body: Internal and external teams adopted the experience, bringing related design assets into one workspace. Stable CDN links and version control also accelerated implementation by letting teams update deployed assets without redeploying their products.

whatScaled: The shared asset model extended into Lottie Creator and the plugins. Its multi-format foundation also expanded CDN delivery and enabled teams to include a broader range of assets inside Motion Systems.

title: LottieFiles Motion Systems
summary: Brought motion standards into one governed system teams could manage, publish, and use across their creative tools.
description:
Building on an initial proof of concept, I led the UX and UI for Motion Systems within LottieFiles Platform. I reshaped it into a cohesive experience that supported the full lifecycle of a Motion System, from initial setup and brand-guide import to managing principles, tokens, easing curves, assets, and other system values, through drafting, publishing, and version history. I also contributed directly to front-end implementation within Platform.

The experience needed to remain consistent across Platform, Lottie Creator, Figma, and After Effects without forcing the same interface into tools with different purposes. I worked directly with the Creator designer, PM, engineers, and Head of Product through hands-on alignment sessions, guiding how the Platform patterns were adapted to creation and plugin workflows. I also reviewed and performed design QA across Platform, Creator, and the plugins to keep the coordinated release cohesive through implementation.

insights.label: Why it mattered
insights.body: Team and Enterprise customers, internal users, and LottieFiles’ motion designers were managing motion standards through incomplete or disconnected systems. We also saw an opportunity to address a broader market gap, since many established design systems still lacked a governed motion layer.

insights.label: Key decision
insights.body: We established one shared model for creating, managing, drafting, publishing, and versioning Motion Systems, then adapted the interface to each tool. The first set of system values was scoped with LottieFiles’ internal Motion Design team so the experience remained useful without becoming overly complex.

insights.label: Outcome
insights.body: Motion Systems launched as a coordinated experience across Platform, Creator, Figma, and After Effects. Cross-product design QA helped preserve the shared model and interaction quality through implementation, and the release received positive feedback from external users. The creation flow also evolved during development, replacing less predictable AI-based brand-guide extraction with Brandfetch data for a more reliable foundation.

whatScaled: The Platform experience for creating, managing, publishing, and versioning Motion Systems became the shared foundation used across Creator and the plugins, connecting governance with the tools where teams created and applied motion.

title: LottieFiles Developer Handoff
summary: Turned fragmented animation implementation into a focused, stack-aware developer handoff.
description:
Customer feedback and product data showed that developers struggled to translate animation assets into the correct production setup. Technical details, implementation requirements, and guidance were spread across different places, creating friction between receiving an asset and shipping it.

With no formal PRD, I aligned directly with the Head of Product on the problem and potential direction. I built an AI-assisted proof of concept to explore a focused, full-page handoff experience, used it to align on the approach, and then developed the concept into a high-fidelity design.

I owned the UX and UI, worked closely with Engineering throughout implementation, and conducted design QA before rollout. The resulting experience brought asset details, technical specifications, setup instructions, and ready-to-use code into one workspace.

insights.label: Why it mattered
insights.body: Developers needed a clearer path from receiving an animation to implementing it correctly. Generic documentation still required them to interpret asset requirements and determine which instructions applied to their development stack.

insights.label: Key decision
insights.body: Instead of presenting the same documentation to everyone, I designed a dynamic integration guide that adapted its setup steps and code to the selected platform, framework, player, and animation features.

insights.label: Outcome
insights.body: The experience entered a phased A/B rollout with a small percentage of users, allowing the team to validate its effectiveness before expanding availability.

title: Lummi Figma plugin
summary: Brought Lummi’s image library directly into Figma.
description: Designed the Lummi Figma plugin around speed, simplicity, and consistency with the web experience. The plugin brought image discovery, categories, filters, creator profiles, quick insertion, and randomized multi-image insertion directly into designers’ existing workflow.

solution: I brought discovery and insertion into one focused plugin, letting designers search, browse, and place single or multiple images without leaving Figma. Shared patterns kept the experience familiar to existing Lummi users.

title: Musho Figma Plugin
summary: Reimagined AI page creation as a conversation.
description: Designed components and product views for the Musho Figma plugin, including an exploration of a chat-based AI workflow. The concept replaced a sequence of isolated actions with a more conversational experience for generating and refining landing-page content.
problem: The existing action-based workflow asked designers to break creative intent into a sequence of isolated commands. Generating and refining a page felt fragmented because each step provided limited context for the larger idea.
solution: I explored a conversational workflow that carried context between prompts. Designers could describe an idea, review the result, and refine the page through one continuous exchange inside Figma.

title: Buenoverse
summary: Made choosing an avatar feel like part of the adventure.
description: Designed the avatar-selection interface for Buenoverse, balancing creative flexibility with a clear and approachable experience. The work focused on navigation, customization, visual feedback, and a cohesive presentation that helped players choose how they entered the world.
problem: The first step into Buenoverse involved a wide range of avatar choices and customization options. Too much complexity risked turning an exciting opening moment into a setup task.
solution: I shaped a visually led selection flow with clear navigation and immediate feedback. Players could explore their options confidently while the interface preserved the playful character of the world they were about to enter.

title: Bueno Drops Figma Plugin
summary: Turned Figma artwork into launch-ready digital collectibles.
description: Led the design of the Bueno Drops Figma Plugin, creating a focused workflow that helped artists turn designs into digital collectibles without coding. I streamlined the flow, designed an accessible interface, and supported both Open and Limited Edition drops from setup through launch.
problem: Artists could create their work in Figma, but publishing it as a digital collectible required technical knowledge and a chain of unfamiliar tools. That gap added friction between creation and launch, especially for less technical creators.
solution: I designed an end-to-end plugin flow that guided artists from selected artwork through edition type, configuration, and launch. A few clear steps reduced the technical burden while preserving control over the final drop.
